evidenceRecords.question: What has the glioblastoma experiment shown?
evidenceRecords.finding: Mitochondrial stress and inhibited tumor growth were observed in preclinical models, not a clinical comparison.

studies.population: Glioblastoma cell and experimental tumor models

evidenceRecords.question: What has the breast cancer experiment shown?
evidenceRecords.finding: The study linked PAK1/Akt effects to growth-arresting autophagy in experimental models.

studies.population: Breast cancer models

evidenceRecords.question: What has the colorectal cancer experiment shown?
evidenceRecords.finding: The study demonstrated WNT-TCF pathway effects in laboratory and tumor models.

studies.population: WNT-dependent human cancer models including colorectal cancer

evidenceRecords.question: What has the liver cancer experiment shown?
evidenceRecords.finding: The study examined cancer-cell death and combination effects with sorafenib in preclinical models.

studies.population: Hepatocellular carcinoma models

evidenceRecords.question: What does the ovarian study show?
evidenceRecords.finding: Mebendazole was tested in cell lines and patient-derived xenografts; these models assess antitumor activity without establishing a treatment effect in patients.

studies.population: Ovarian cancer models including cisplatin-resistant tumors

evidenceRecords.question: What did the recurrent-glioblastoma trial find?
evidenceRecords.finding: Nine-month survival was 36.6% with temozolomide–mebendazole and 45% with lomustine–mebendazole, below the 55% benchmark; both arms included mebendazole.

studies.design: Randomized comparison of two mebendazole-containing regimens
studies.population: 88 adults with recurrent glioblastoma

evidenceRecords.notes: Neither arm reached the prespecified 55% benchmark; both contained mebendazole.

evidenceRecords.question: What has head-and-neck research demonstrated?
evidenceRecords.finding: The oral-cell study found changes in migration and cell-state markers, not clinical tumor response or survival.

studies.population: Oral cancer and dysplastic oral cell lines

evidenceRecords.question: Has it been shown to treat ovarian cancer in people?
evidenceRecords.finding: The cited ovarian study tested cancer cells and animal tumors, not people with ovarian cancer.

studies.population: A2780 and SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells and experimental tumors

evidenceRecords.question: What improved in the reported series?
evidenceRecords.finding: Patients reported better working memory, concentration and executive function; four discontinued treatment, including two with hypotension or dizziness.

studies.population: 12 people with Long COVID cognitive symptoms

evidenceRecords.design: Uncontrolled guanfacine plus N-acetylcysteine case series
evidenceRecords.safety: Two discontinued because of hypotension/dizziness; two for unspecified reasons.

evidenceRecords.question: Has it prevented breast-cancer spread in patients?
evidenceRecords.finding: The cited work reduced pulmonary metastasis in mice; it did not test prevention of metastasis in patients.

studies.population: Basal breast cancer models

evidenceRecords.question: What did the colorectal program demonstrate?
evidenceRecords.finding: It linked CCR5 blockade to macrophage changes and tumor-cell death, with clinical activity in an early pilot; a randomized survival advantage was not tested.

studies.design: Human tumor experiments and phase I pilot study
studies.population: Colorectal cancer liver metastases

evidenceRecords.design: Phase I translational study with ex vivo experiments
evidenceRecords.notes: Tumor-microenvironment changes do not supply a randomized survival comparison.

evidenceRecords.question: What is known in pancreatic cancer?
evidenceRecords.finding: Maraviroc reduced CCL5-driven invasive behavior in cell experiments; that study did not measure patient outcomes.

studies.population: Pancreatic cancer cells

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve glioblastoma outcomes?
evidenceRecords.finding: The single-arm 36-patient study reported 66% progression-free at six months but concluded that improvement was not demonstrated.

studies.population: 36 patients with glioblastoma

evidenceRecords.notes: Single-arm adjunctive atorvastatin with chemoradiation; did not establish improved PFS6.

evidenceRecords.question: Did it slow prostate tumor proliferation?
evidenceRecords.finding: Among 160 randomized men, short preoperative atorvastatin did not significantly lower overall Ki-67 or PSA compared with placebo.

studies.population: 160 men randomized; 158 completed follow-up

evidenceRecords.notes: Overall Ki67 and PSA results were negative; exploratory subgroup effects must stay labeled subgroup.

evidenceRecords.question: What happened in the breast study?
evidenceRecords.finding: Overall Ki-67 decreased by 7.6% (p=0.39); a larger decrease in the HMGCR-positive subgroup was exploratory and not a survival result.

studies.population: 50 patients enrolled with invasive breast cancer

effects.endpoint: Ki67 relative change in HMGCR-positive subgroup

evidenceRecords.notes: Two-week presurgical window; no placebo; proliferation biomarker is not recurrence or survival.

evidenceRecords.question: Has it treated AML in this evidence?
evidenceRecords.finding: The cited study observed cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis in leukemia cell lines, not clinical remission or survival.

studies.population: K562 and HL60 leukemia cells

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve phototherapy results?
evidenceRecords.finding: In the small randomized trial, adding atorvastatin to narrow-band UVB did not significantly improve VASI versus UVB alone.

evidenceRecords.question: Did pigmentation improve?
evidenceRecords.finding: The pilot reported substantial improvement in three patients, slight improvement in one and no improvement in one over six months.

studies.population: Five patients with active disseminated vitiligo

evidenceRecords.question: What was reported in Long COVID?
evidenceRecords.finding: The 24 completers reported symptom improvements on valacyclovir–celecoxib with or without Paxlovid; convenience sampling and multiple drugs prevent attribution to celecoxib.

studies.population: 24 completers receiving valacyclovir–celecoxib with or without Paxlovid

evidenceRecords.notes: Combination treatment and completer selection prevent drug-specific causal inference.

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve ovarian-cancer survival?
evidenceRecords.finding: DoCaCel found no significant progression-free or overall survival advantage, with interpretation limited by premature celecoxib discontinuation.

studies.population: 196 eligible patients with epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer

evidenceRecords.notes: Randomized phase II study found no significant PFS or OS advantage; early discontinuation matters.

evidenceRecords.question: Did it relieve radiotherapy mouth symptoms?
evidenceRecords.finding: In 40 randomized patients, celecoxib did not reduce oral mucositis severity, pain, dietary compromise or opioid use.

studies.population: 40 head-and-neck cancer patients receiving radiotherapy

evidenceRecords.endpoint: Radiotherapy oral mucositis and related symptoms
evidenceRecords.notes: Supportive-care trial; not a cancer response endpoint.

evidenceRecords.question: Did it prevent breast-cancer recurrence?
evidenceRecords.finding: REACT found no disease-free survival advantage: hazard ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.17).

studies.population: 2639 patients with primary breast cancer

evidenceRecords.question: Did it prevent colon-cancer recurrence?
evidenceRecords.finding: Overall disease-free survival was not significantly improved (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.03); a preplanned PIK3CA subgroup analysis reported a more favorable result.

studies.population: Resected stage III colon cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy

studies.design: Preplanned molecular subgroup analysis of randomized trial
studies.population: Patients from CALGB/SWOG 80702 with tumor sequencing

evidenceRecords.notes: PIK3CA molecular analysis is a subgroup of CALGB/SWOG 80702, not a second independent family.

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve the pancreatic chemotherapy combination?
evidenceRecords.finding: The phase II report concluded that celecoxib did not appear to add activity to gemcitabine and cisplatin.

studies.population: Advanced pancreatic cancer

evidenceRecords.question: What happened in the liver-cancer pilot?
evidenceRecords.finding: Median survival was 15 months with TACE plus celecoxib and lanreotide versus 7.5 months with TACE alone; adding two drugs prevents assigning the benefit to celecoxib alone.

studies.population: 71 people with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma

evidenceRecords.notes: Two agents were added to TACE; the effect cannot be assigned to celecoxib alone.

evidenceRecords.question: Has it treated ovarian cancer in patients?
evidenceRecords.finding: The cited study measured signaling and invasion in cells and mouse tumors, not patient response or survival.

studies.population: Ovarian cancer cell lines and mouse tumors

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve treatment-resistant depression?
evidenceRecords.finding: Six weeks of adjunctive minocycline did not significantly improve depression severity versus placebo in the 168-person analysis.

studies.population: 173 randomized; 168 intention-to-treat participants with TRD

evidenceRecords.question: Did the Parkinson’s pilot establish slower progression?
evidenceRecords.finding: The exploratory follow-up assessed whether larger efficacy testing was feasible; it did not establish disease modification, and lower tolerability was a concern.

studies.population: Early Parkinson disease

evidenceRecords.question: Did it improve negative symptoms?
evidenceRecords.finding: BeneMin found no significant effect: the negative-symptom difference was −0.19 points (95% CI −1.23 to 0.85).

evidenceRecords.question: Did it slow Alzheimer’s decline?
evidenceRecords.finding: Two years of treatment did not slow cognitive or daily-function decline; the higher 400 mg daily dose was poorly tolerated.

studies.population: 554 randomized; 544 eligible people with mild Alzheimer disease

evidenceRecords.question: Did it delay multiple sclerosis?
evidenceRecords.finding: After a first demyelinating event, adjusted six-month conversion risk was 18.5 percentage points lower (95% CI 3.7 to 33.3); the 24-month difference was not significant.

studies.population: 142 people after a first demyelinating event

evidenceRecords.notes: First demyelinating event population; 24-month difference not significant.

evidenceRecords.question: What happened in ALS?
evidenceRecords.finding: Functional scores declined faster with minocycline: −1.30 versus −1.04 ALSFRS-R points per month in the placebo group.

studies.design: Multicenter randomized placebo-controlled phase III trial

evidenceRecords.question: Did it stop vitiligo spreading?
evidenceRecords.finding: In a 50-person comparison with dexamethasone, disease activity decreased in both groups without a significant difference; there was no placebo arm.

studies.population: 50 people with actively spreading vitiligo

evidenceRecords.notes: Disease activity decreased in both groups; no placebo and no significant between-group difference.
